doc.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: Best musical situations: McCoy Tyner quartet, his father and Roots
summary: He calls the McCoy Tyner quartet his current favorite and describes his saxophone-quartet band Roots with Benny Golson and others.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: What’s the best — I don’t know if you can think of this quite offhand, but what’s one of the best musical situations that you’ve been involved in so far?
One of the best? Oh there are a few. Well the one with McCoy is great. For me it’s great. I’m in a quartet situation so there’s a lot of freedom and it’s, again, playing with McCoy.

This is great. This is one of the best right now. Outside of what I do myself, I think this is probably my favorite thing right now. And I love playing with my father when we do that. I also have worked with the band called Roots, which is like a saxophone quartet with a rhythm section. Actually the original band was great, it originally was Don Pullen on piano, we had Buster Williams on bass and we had Idris Muhammad in the rhythm section. Now it’s Ed Thigpen, which he’s absolutely wonderful drummer, and Buster and George Kape, or I’m sorry, Kirk Lightsey. And then there’s Benny Golson, Arthur Blythe, Nathan Davis and myself. And so that band, when we do some things is — because being with Benny Golson and playing those Benny Golson arrangements and things, so it’s really great, so I like doing that.
